children.name: Haematopus
children.description: Noisy pied waders of rocky shores. The bright orange bill is used to prise open mussels or stab open cockles — each individual learns one technique and uses it for life. Their loud piping calls are a defining sound of the Swedish archipelago coastline.

children.name: Haematopus ostralegus
children.description: The Eurasian oystercatcher or European oystercatcher, also known as the common pied oystercatcher, or just oystercatcher, is a wader in the oystercatcher bird family Haematopodidae. It has striking black and white plumage, a long straight orange-red bill, red eyes and relatively short dull pink legs. The sexes are similar in appearance but the bill of the female is longer than that of the male.

children.name: Haematopus palliatus
children.description: The American oystercatcher (Haematopus palliatus), occasionally called the American pied oystercatcher, is a member of family Haematopodidae.

children.name: Haematopus bachmani
children.description: The black oystercatcher (Haematopus bachmani) is a conspicuous black bird found on the shoreline of western North America, ranging from the Aleutian Islands of Alaska to the coast of the Baja California peninsula.

children.name: Haematopus moquini
children.description: The African oystercatcher or African black oystercatcher (Haematopus moquini) is a large charismatic wader resident to the mainland coasts and offshore islands of southern Africa.

children.name: Haematopus fuliginosus
children.description: The sooty oystercatcher (Haematopus fuliginosus) is a species of oystercatcher.

children.name: Haematopus longirostris
children.description: The pied oystercatcher (Haematopus longirostris) is a species of oystercatcher.

children.name: Haematopus unicolor
children.description: The variable oystercatcher is a species of wader in the family Haematopodidae. It is endemic to New Zealand. The Māori name is tōrea-pango.

children.name: Haematopus finschi
children.description: The South Island oystercatcher or South Island pied oystercatcher is one of two common oystercatcher species found in New Zealand. Its name is often contracted to the acronym "SIPO". The indigenous Māori name is tōrea.

children.name: Haematopus chathamensis
children.description: The Chatham Islands oystercatcher (Haematopus chathamensis) or tōrea tai, formerly known as the Chatham oystercatcher, is a species of oystercatcher. It is a wading bird endemic to the Chatham Islands, New Zealand. This species is rated by the IUCN as endangered, and has a current population of 310 to 325 birds (2004 census). The main threat is from introduced predators.

children.name: Haematopus leucopodus
children.description: The Magellanic oystercatcher (Haematopus leucopodus) is a species of wader in the family Haematopodidae.

children.name: Haematopus meadewaldoi
children.description: The Canary Islands oystercatcher, Canarian oystercatcher, or Canarian black oystercatcher (Haematopus meadewaldoi) is an extinct shorebird of uncertain taxonomy endemic to Fuerteventura, Lanzarote, and their offshore islets (Islote de Lobos and the Chinijo Archipelago) in the Canary Islands in Spain. Its population declined sharply beginning in the 1800s due primarily to overharvesting by humans of their shared food sources in the intertidal zone. Since the 1940s, the Canary Islands oystercatcher has been considered to be extinct.

children.name: Haematopus ophthalmicus
children.description: The eastern far-eastern populations of the oystercatcher complex breeding in Kamchatka and northeast Asia, sometimes treated as a distinct race, with a very prominent orange eye-ring. Coastal and estuarine.
